outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the question has not been settled in either direction: no ZF-without-AC refutation survives (McCallum's January 2026 preprint on Σ₁ embeddings of Vλ₊₃ was withdrawn by its author in August 2026), and the consistency results found (Schlutzenberg's V_λ₊₂ result, published 2024 after a 2020 preprint; Jeon's cofinal ZF⁻ result, June 2024) concern changed embeddings or changed base theories, and are relative to I₀.
problem_asks: The bullet asks whether, with the axiom of choice not assumed, a nontrivial elementary embedding j: V→V can exist. Parts: (1) EXISTENCE: is there a base theory without AC (ZF with Separation and Replacement for formulas mentioning j, written ZF(j) in Hamkins et al. 2011; or NBG/Morse–Kelley without choice, with j a proper class) that is consistent with a nontrivial elementary j: V→V? (2) NON-EXISTENCE: does the same AC-free base theory prove that no nontrivial elementary j: V→V exists? (3) DEFINABILITY: the bullet does not restrict j, so both arbitrary class j and j definable from parameters are asked; the definable case is a sub-part of (1) and (2). (4) BASE THEORY: the bullet does not name one; the readings in the literature (ZF(j), NBG without AC) are different framings of the same question, and the record flags where a result uses a different base. Not asked by the bullet but relevant to scope: whether the answer changes if j is cofinal, if Powerset is dropped, or if the embedding is restricted to Vλ₊₂ or Vλ₊₃.

events.what_happened: Kenneth Kunen, 'Elementary embeddings and infinitary combinatorics', Journal of Symbolic Logic 36 (1971) 407–413. Under ZFC, no nontrivial elementary j: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂ exists; Kunen remarks the argument can be formalised in Morse–Kelley, which gives the V→V form under AC. Suzuki's JSL extract dates the result to 1970; the journal year is used here.
events.delivers: Under AC (ZFC; Morse–Kelley for the V→V form), no nontrivial elementary j: V→V and no nontrivial j: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂. This is the answer to the question with AC assumed, which is why the bullet asks about dropping AC.
events.remains: Every part of problem_asks in the AC-free setting: whether a base theory without AC admits or refutes a nontrivial j: V→V.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of record); individual referees not named in the sources I could see

events.what_happened: Akira Suzuki, 'No elementary embedding from V into V is definable from parameters', Journal of Symbolic Logic 64(4) (December 1999), pp. 1591–1594, Nagoya University. Works in ZF, without AC, for embeddings defined by a formula with a parameter; proves no nontrivial elementary j: V→V is so definable (a theorem scheme). I found no earlier preprint; the journal issue date is the only date available. The Cambridge page also shows a 'published online 12 March 2014' date, which I take as an online-archive date, not the first written argument.
events.delivers: In ZF (no AC): there is no nontrivial elementary j: V→V definable from parameters (a schema, per Hamkins et al. and the FOM summaries). This restricts to definable embeddings; it does not cover arbitrary class j.
events.remains: The arbitrary-class (non-definable) case in ZF(j) and in NBG without AC; the consistency side is untouched.

checked_by.who: Journal of Symbolic Logic (refereed journal of record)
Joel David Hamkins, Greg Kirmayer, Norman Lewis Perlmutter
checked_by.qualification: Set theorists; the survey is written for the field
checked_by.what_they_did: Restate Suzuki's definable-case result as settled in ZF and say the class case remains Question 38

events.direction: Cuts against existence, but only for embeddings definable from parameters.

events.what_happened: Joel David Hamkins, Greg Kirmayer, Norman Lewis Perlmutter, 'Generalizations of the Kunen Inconsistency', arXiv 1106.1951. First submitted 10 June 2011; v2 27 May 2012, revised after referee suggestions; no journal reference listed on arXiv. Survey plus new results. Poses Question 38: is it consistent without AC that j: V→V is a nontrivial elementary embedding of the universe (in NGB, j a class)? Calls it the principal open question in the area. Per the search-result summary of the paper (I read only the abstract, which does not contain the question), the definable case is settled in ZF by Theorem 32.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jun 2011; v2 27 May 2012 (referee suggestions, expository changes).
events.delivers: Restates the AC-free question for arbitrary class j as open (Question 38) and records that the known refutation arguments either use AC (the stationary partition theorem) or assume j definable. Establishes, in ZF, the definable-j case (Theorem 32, per summary).
events.remains: Everything except the definable case: whether a non-definable nontrivial j: V→V is consistent without AC, or refutable in ZF(j) or NBG without AC.

checked_by.who: Joel David Hamkins, Greg Kirmayer, Norman Lewis Perlmutter
checked_by.qualification: Set theorists, Hamkins a senior figure in the field; I did not verify their credentials beyond this
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote the survey and posed Question 38

events.direction: Frames the question as open for class j; neither cuts for nor against it. Refutes the definable case in ZF.

events.what_happened: Jindřich Zapletal, 'A new proof of Kunen's inconsistency', arXiv math/9309207, submitted 15 September 1993; Proceedings of the AMS 124 (1996) 2203–2204. Uses elementary pcf (a fact from Shelah's theory of possible cofinalities, which uses AC) to show there is no transitive M with j: V→M, j(λ)=λ>crit(j), j''λ∈M.
events.revisions: v1 15 Sep 1993 only; published Proc. AMS 1996.
events.delivers: A second ZFC proof of the AC-based Kunen theorem, for embeddings into transitive M, including the case that j''λ is not in M. Relies on pcf, which needs AC.
events.remains: The AC-free question for j: V→V, for which pcf gives no help as the author uses it.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record); communicated by Andreas R. Blass per the AMS listing

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'Even ordinals and the Kunen inconsistency', arXiv 2006.01084, submitted 1 June 2020 (v2 2 June 2020; v3 18 Feb 2021). Abstract: works in the choiceless setting, under choiceless large cardinal axioms; (i) periodicity of the cumulative hierarchy, even vs odd ranks; (ii) ultrafilter structure under a weak Ultrapower Axiom; (iii) assuming DC, an elementary j: Vλ₊₃→Vλ₊₃ implies Con(ZFC+I₀). It notes that by a result of Schlutzenberg an embedding Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂ does not suffice for these consequences.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jun 2020; v2 2 Jun 2020; v3 18 Feb 2021 (current).
events.delivers: Conditional results under choiceless large-cardinal hypotheses: periodicity, ultrafilter structure, and a consistency-strength bound from a Vλ₊₃ embedding. It does not establish or refute a nontrivial j: V→V without AC.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against: all results are conditional on choiceless large-cardinal hypotheses. The abstract reads the Kunen inconsistency as the reason the choiceless hierarchy exists.

events.what_happened: Rupert McCallum, 'The choiceless cardinals are inconsistent', arXiv 1712.09678, first posted 27 December 2017. Abstract: 'We give a proof of the Kunen inconsistency in ZF.' Withdrawn: v4 (25 Feb 2018) and v5 (8 Oct 2020) are marked withdrawn; the comment on the listing reads 'There is a flaw in the proof of the first lemma.' A FOM post (Dec 2017; I could not open it, so only a search-snippet summary) identifies the flaw as Lemma 0.4, which wrongly assumes N ∩ HOD = HOD.
events.revisions: v1 27 Dec 2017; v2 2 Jan 2018; v3 7 Jan 2018; v4 25 Feb 2018 (withdrawn); v5 8 Oct 2020 (withdrawn).
events.delivers: Claimed a ZF-only proof of the Kunen inconsistency, which as stated is for the Vλ₊₂ form and therefore stronger than the V→V form. Withdrawn, so it establishes nothing as a result.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, given the withdrawal.

checked_by.who: FOM mailing list discussion (Dec 2017); poster identity not verified in my reading
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified an error in Lemma 0.4 per a search-snippet summary

events.doubts: The author withdrew the paper twice; the listing says the first lemma is flawed; a FOM post (per search-snippet summary) gives a specific error in Lemma 0.4 (N ∩ HOD = HOD assumed without justification). The withdrawal in v4 predates the Schlutzenberg 2020 consistency result for the Vλ₊₂ form, which the withdrawn paper's claim would contradict.

withdrawn.what: v4 (25 Feb 2018) and v5 (8 Oct 2020) marked withdrawn by the author; comment: 'There is a flaw in the proof of the first lemma.'

events.direction: Claimed to refute the Vλ₊₂ embedding in ZF, which would cut against existence; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Farmer Schlutzenberg, 'On the consistency of ZF with an elementary embedding from Vλ₊₂ into Vλ₊₂', arXiv 2006.01077 (v1 1 June 2020; v4 18 March 2024), published Journal of Mathematical Logic, article 2450013, DOI 10.1142/S0219061324500132. Main result: assuming ZF + I₀,λ + 'λ is an even ordinal', there is a proper-class inner model M ⊇ Vλ₊₁ satisfying ZF + I₀,λ + an elementary k: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂. Also shows ZFC + 'λ even' + I₀,λ gives A# for each A in Vλ₊₁. The abstract states that no proof of Kunen's theorem from ZF alone has been found. Goldberg is credited with removing the extra assumption that Vλ₊₁# exists.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jun 2020; v2 8 Jun 2020; v3 11 Jun 2020; v4 18 Mar 2024 (reorganised, generalised to relevant triples, minor corrections). Journal listing: online 16 Mar 2024 per a search-snippet of an aggregator; the publisher page returned 403 to my fetch, so the journal date is not checked. Wikipedia (Reinhardt cardinal article) dates the peer-reviewed article to 2025; see disputes.
events.delivers: Relative consistency, over ZF + I₀,λ, of ZF with an elementary embedding of Vλ₊₂ into itself, for λ even. Restrictions: the embedding is into Vλ₊₂, not V; the result is conditional on I₀,λ; the witness is an inner model of ZF, which is itself a ZF model containing the embedding. It does not decide whether ZF proves the nonexistence of j: V→V.
events.remains: The V→V form in ZF(j) or NBG without AC; the unconditional question for Vλ₊₂ also (the abstract calls the ZF question open).

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Logic (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published after refereeing (date per aggregator; see disputes)
Observed the extra assumption Vλ₊₁# existence was unnecessary, acknowledged in the published abstract

events.direction: Cuts toward consistency of an AC-free embedding of Vλ₊₂, conditional on I₀,λ. Its scope is Vλ₊₂, not V→V.
events.object: A proper-class transitive inner model M ⊇ Vλ₊₁ with M ⊨ ZF + I₀,λ + 'there is an elementary k: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂'. A relative consistency result from I₀,λ; the witness is not explicit.

events.what_happened: Joel David Hamkins, 'The Wholeness Axioms and V=HOD', arXiv math/9902079, submitted 13 February 1999. Abstract: Corazza's Wholeness Axioms axiomatise an elementary j: V→V in ZFC with j added as a symbol, without Replacement for j-formulas; the paper proves that if WA₀ is consistent then it is consistent with V=HOD. Consistency strength below I₃.
events.delivers: Consistency of a weakened j-theory (WA₀) with V=HOD. The restriction is that Replacement does not apply to j-formulas, which is the very scheme Kunen's argument uses. Does not address ZF(j) with full Replacement for j-formulas, nor NBG with a class j.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, because the theory is changed.
events.direction: Neither: a consistency result for a changed theory with j.

events.what_happened: Dmytro Taranovsky, 'Elementarily self-embeddable models of ZFC', a personal web note (MIT server). Per a search-snippet summary of the page (the page returned 404 to my fetch): ZFC with a j symbol but without full Separation or Replacement for j-formulas; results range from conservativity over ZFC to equiconsistency with large cardinals, depending on which fragments are kept.
events.revisions: Dated February 2020, modified May 2020 (per search-snippet summary).
events.delivers: Results for ZFC with a j symbol and weakened j-schemes. The restriction is the weakening of the j-schemes, so it is a changed theory, not ZF(j) with full schemes.
events.doubts: I could not open the page, so its claims are from the search-snippet summary only.
events.direction: Neither: results for a changed theory.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'Measurable cardinals and choiceless axioms', arXiv 2106.05916, first posted 10 June 2021 (v2 15 July 2021; v3 2 Nov 2021). Abstract (v1): if there is an elementary embedding from the universe to itself, then there is a proper class of measurable successor cardinals. v3 adds that Kunen's refutation uses AC and asks what the embedding implies without AC.
events.delivers: Conditional: if a nontrivial j: V→V exists (without AC assumed), there is a proper class of λ with λ⁺ measurable. It does not establish existence or nonexistence of j.
events.direction: Neither: a conditional consequence of an assumed j.

events.what_happened: Hanul Jeon, 'On a cofinal Reinhardt embedding without Powerset', arXiv 2406.10698, submitted 15 June 2024; Fundamenta Mathematicae 270 (2025) 177–200, DOI 10.4064/fm240829-20-6. Abstract: answers Matthews' question positively: ZF⁻ (ZF without Powerset) is consistent with a nontrivial cofinal elementary j: V→V. The consistency follows from ZFC + I₀, witnessed by Schlutzenberg's model of ZF with k: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂. In the v4 body, Definition 2.1 says ZFC⁻ is ZF⁻ plus the well-ordering principle, and 'we use the Well-ordering principle instead of Choice'.
events.delivers: Relative consistency (over ZFC + I₀) of a nontrivial cofinal j: V→V with a base theory without Powerset. Restrictions: cofinal (Matthews' earlier embedding, which is not cofinal, is a different case; per the v4 body (Theorem 1.6), Matthews' result needs I₁(λ)); base theory without Powerset; the v4 body's base is ZFC⁻, which includes the well-ordering principle, so the main result may not be AC-free. The abstract names ZF⁻. Whether the main result is AC-free depends on which base theory is meant.
events.remains: Whether a base theory with Powerset and without AC (ZF or NBG) admits a nontrivial j: V→V; whether non-cofinal j is consistent in the AC-free setting; and whether Question 38 is answered at all.

checked_by.who: Fundamenta Mathematicae (refereed journal of record); the acknowledgements thank 'the reviewer for a meticulous and helpful review'
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the author also credits Karagila (CHEESE workshop) and Hayut

events.doubts: Base-theory discrepancy: the abstract says ZF⁻, the body's Definition 2.1 says ZFC⁻ with well-ordering, and the search summary says versions differ. If the main result is in ZFC⁻, it assumes a global choice principle and does not answer the AC-free question. Also relative to I₀ with ZFC as metatheory, and restricted to cofinal j.
events.direction: Cuts toward existence (consistency), for a changed base theory and a cofinal embedding.
events.object: A model of ZF⁻ (ZFC⁻ in the body) with a cofinal nontrivial j: V→V, obtained from Schlutzenberg's model of ZF + k: Vλ₊₂→Vλ₊₂ under I₀. A relative consistency result; the witness is not explicit.

events.what_happened: Farmer Schlutzenberg, 'Large cardinals and the Axiom of Choice', talk at the International Congress of Basic Science 2025, Beijing (13–25 July 2025), listed in TU Wien repositum (handle 20.500.12708/224925) as published 13 July 2025. Talk abstract only: the large cardinal notion Kunen refuted under ZFC is consistent with ZF without AC, assuming well-studied large cardinals are consistent; 'modulo these assumptions, Kunen's proof really does require AC'. Refers to the 2020/2024 paper.
events.delivers: Restates the conditional V_λ₊₂ result from the 2020/2024 paper as a claim that Kunen's proof requires AC, modulo large-cardinal assumptions. No new argument is shown in the abstract.
events.remains: The unconditional question; the V→V form in ZF(j) or NBG without AC.
events.doubts: Talk abstract only; not refereed; the 'Choice is necessary' claim is conditional on I₀ consistency and concerns Vλ₊₂.
events.direction: Conditional claim that AC is needed for Kunen's Vλ₊₂ theorem. Scope is Vλ₊₂.

events.what_happened: Farmer Schlutzenberg, 'Large cardinals beyond the bounds of the Axiom of Choice', talk at the Australasian Association for Logic 2025, Brisbane (3–7 November 2025), listed in TU Wien repositum (handle 20.500.12708/224923) as published 7 November 2025. Talk abstract only: recent work demonstrates that, assuming I₀ is consistent, Choice is in fact necessary for Kunen's result.
events.delivers: Conditional restatement (on I₀ consistency) that Choice is necessary for Kunen's Vλ₊₂ result. The 'recent work' is not identified in the abstract.
events.remains: The unconditional question, and the V→V form.
events.doubts: Talk abstract only; the 'recent work' it cites is not identified; the conditional nature is explicit.
events.direction: Conditional claim that AC is needed for Kunen's Vλ₊₂ result.

events.what_happened: Marwan Salam Mohammed, 'Reinhardt Cardinals and Eventually Dominating Functions', arXiv 2505.00637, submitted 1 May 2025 (single version). Background theory ZF(j) = ZFC(j) without AC. Sections 2–4 and Theorem 3.10 are in ZF(j); Section 5 uses AC to show there are (j,δ)-small sets, and Corollary 5.4 concludes ZFC(j) is inconsistent: a new proof of Kunen's inconsistency. Introduction: 'Crucial to his proof was the use of the Axiom of Choice (AC) and it is still unknown if an inconsistency exists without it.'
events.delivers: A new proof of the AC-based Kunen inconsistency for ZFC(j). Theorem 3.10 and the Section 2–4 material are proved in ZF(j) without AC, but the author states that the inconsistency itself is not proved without AC.
events.remains: The AC-free question for ZF(j) and for NBG without AC, which the author says is still unknown.
events.direction: Neither: a ZFC proof, and the author says the AC-free question is open.

events.what_happened: Juan P. Aguilera, Joan Bagaria, Philipp Lücke, 'Large cardinals, structural reflection, and the HOD Conjecture', arXiv 2411.11568 (v1 18 Nov 2024; v4 16 Sep 2025). Introduces exacting and ultraexacting cardinals; consistency with ZFC relative to an I₀ embedding; exacting cardinal implies V ≠ HOD.
events.delivers: Nothing about a nontrivial j: V→V without AC: the paper concerns exacting and ultraexacting cardinals and HOD. Discarded as adjacent.
events.direction: Neither: no bearing on j: V→V.

events.what_happened: Rupert McCallum, 'Inconsistency of Reinhardt cardinals with ZF', arXiv 2601.10231, first submitted 15 January 2026; v2 12 February 2026; v3 23 August 2026 is marked 'This paper has been withdrawn by Rupert McCallum.' Abstract (v1/v2): a proof that a nontrivial Σ₁-elementary j: Vλ₊₃ ≺ Vλ₊₃ is inconsistent with ZF; introduces large cardinal properties of consistency strength between I₃ and I₂. Section 4 contains the proof; Theorem 4.1 (v2 html) states the non-existence of a nontrivial Σ₁-elementary j: Vλ₊₃ ≺ Vλ₊₃ in ZF. The v2 proof uses Skolem functions chosen to be continuous in the product topology (Section 4). The v3 comment: 'An issue has been identified with the claim about continuity of Skolem functions, in the final section of the paper. Although I will attempt to repair this problem, I thought it best to indicate that an error has been found.'
events.revisions: v1 15 Jan 2026; v2 12 Feb 2026; v3 23 Aug 2026 (withdrawn).
events.delivers: Claimed ZF-inconsistency of a Σ₁-elementary embedding of Vλ₊₃ into itself, which would refute the Reinhardt-type hypothesis at a level of the hierarchy; the withdrawn v3 page carries no statement. Wikipedia's Reinhardt cardinal article says the claim was never peer-reviewed and that the preprint was withdrawn in August 2026 because the author found an error. The paper itself describes the embedding as Σ₁ into Vλ₊₃, not j: V→V.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, because the claim is withdrawn; the Vλ₊₃ case is also not the V→V case. Whether a restriction of a nontrivial j: V→V to Vλ₊₃ would be covered is a judging-pass question; Wikipedia treats the preprint as bearing on Reinhardt cardinals.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author for an error in the continuity of Skolem functions in the final section, which the v2 proof uses. The author says he intends to repair it. No independent expert engagement found; Wikipedia says never peer-reviewed. A third-party AI-generated review (themoonlight.io) describes the paper as proving a wider inconsistency of choiceless large cardinals; I could not open it (HTTP 429), and the review predates or ignores the withdrawal.

The fetched page does not mention Kunen's inconsistency, Reinhardt cardinals, or ZF refuting them.

events.what_happened: Stanford's UQ question 101, 'Supercompact and Reinhardt cardinals without choice' (posted 22 April 2012), received AI-model answers listed 1 August to 18 September 2025. Question 1 asks whether every uniformly supercompact cardinal is Reinhardt; Question 2 asks its consistency strength. Answers I read: o3 (o3-2025-04-16), main claim: 'Yes. In ZF a "uniformly supercompact" cardinal is automatically Reinhardt.' UQ status: UQ Validated, human verification pending. o4-mini (o4-mini-2025-04-16): 'In ZF alone it is an open problem whether a uniform supercompact κ must carry a nontrivial j:V→V (i.e. be Reinhardt).' UQ Validated; human verification failed. Gemini 2.5 Pro (Google), per the question page: the notion of uniform supercompactness is inconsistent with ZF alone; UQ validation failed. The page also lists GPT-5, o3 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude Opus 4, DeepSeek R1 and K2-Think with validation statuses; I did not read those answers.
events.revisions: Model answers listed 1 Aug 2025 to 18 Sep 2025 (listed timestamps).
events.delivers: No result established. The answers concern a neighbouring question (uniformly supercompact cardinals and Reinhardt cardinals in ZF), not the bullet's question as stated. o3 claims an implication in the existence direction for that neighbour; o4-mini calls the question open; Gemini 2.5 Pro makes a claim about a notion, not the bullet's j. None of the answers is human-verified in the sources I saw.

checked_by.what_they_did: Marked o3 and o4-mini 'UQ Validated' and Gemini 2.5 Pro 'Failed UQ Validation'

disputes.summary: Schlutzenberg's peer-reviewed article: the Wikipedia Reinhardt article says a 2025 peer-reviewed article for which he won the Hausdorff Medal shows the V_λ₊₂ embedding consistent with ZF. The Journal of Mathematical Logic listing (search snippet, Pub Date 2024-03-16) gives 2024. The publisher page returned 403. The Hausdorff Medal Wikipedia page lists recipients through 2024 (Goldberg) and nothing for 2025 or 2026; the Vera Fischer document Wikipedia cites was not retrieved. The 2025 Hausdorff award is therefore unverified.

Jeon's base theory: the abstract (fetched from arxiv abs) names ZF⁻ for the consistency result. The v4 body (Definition 2.1) defines ZFC⁻ as ZF⁻ plus the well-ordering principle and says 'we use the Well-ordering principle instead of Choice'; search summaries say the versions differ in naming. If the main result is in ZFC⁻, it does not answer the AC-free question.

McCallum's January 2026 preprint: Wikipedia's Reinhardt article and the arXiv v3 page both say withdrawn in August 2026 for an error. A third-party AI-generated review (themoonlight.io; not opened, HTTP 429) and a search-result summary describe the preprint as showing a wider inconsistency of choiceless large cardinals, including Reinhardt cardinals, and one search summary said the question was 'largely answered in the negative'. These readings are not supported by the withdrawn record and should not be used.
Kunen's result: Suzuki's JSL extract says Kunen showed the result in 1970; the JSL volume is 1971 (vol. 36, pp. 407–413). The record uses 1971 as the journal year.

Two AI answers on the same UQ question disagree: o3 says that in ZF a uniformly supercompact cardinal is automatically Reinhardt; o4-mini says it is open. Both show 'UQ Validated'; neither is human-verified.

Landscape survey (Srivastava): the arXiv abstract page gives 'submitted 3 May 2022', while the HTML version history begins 31 August 2021. Not an event in this record; noted because the survey is cited as an open-status source in the summary.

summary: Result: the bullet's question, read as either the existence or the non-existence form for arbitrary class j without AC, is still open on every source I could read. The fixed points are: the Wikipedia list entry (Set theory section, no footnote, links to the Reinhardt cardinal article) is confirmed; Kunen (1971) settles the AC case; Suzuki (1999) settles the definable case in ZF. The events since 26 January 2024 are: Jeon (June 2024), a relative consistency of ZF⁻ with a cofinal j: V→V, relative to ZFC + I₀, whose base theory is ZF⁻ in the abstract but ZFC⁻ with well-ordering in the v4 body, so it may not be AC-free and changes the theory (no Powerset) and the embedding (cofinal); Schlutzenberg's Vλ₊₂ consistency result, first posted 2020 and published in JML in 2024 (the publication date is unverified), conditional on I₀,λ and about Vλ₊₂ rather than V; two 2025 Schlutzenberg talk abstracts restating 'Choice is necessary' conditionally for Kunen's Vλ₊₂ result; Mohammed (May 2025), a ZFC(j) proof of Kunen's inconsistency that states the AC-free question is unknown; and McCallum's January 2026 preprint claiming ZF-inconsistency of a Σ₁ embedding of Vλ₊₃, withdrawn by its author on 23 August 2026 because an error was found in the continuity of Skolem functions in the final section. Wikipedia's Reinhardt article (last edited 7 September 2026) says no peer-reviewed refutation of Reinhardt cardinals in ZF alone exists as of August 2026. Nothing in the sources resolves the question. Close calls: (a) Jeon could be read as the consistency side settled, but only for a changed theory and possibly not AC-free; (b) McCallum's withdrawn claim, if it held, would plausibly refute the Reinhardt-type hypothesis in ZF by restriction, since Wikipedia reads it that way, but the author withdrew it and the Σ₁ Vλ₊₃ case is not the V→V case as stated; (c) Suzuki settles the definable case in ZF, but the bullet does not restrict to definable j, and Hamkins et al. treat Question 38 as the class case; (d) Schlutzenberg's 2025 'Choice is necessary' claims are conditional on I₀ and about Vλ₊₂. AI involvement: I found no system credited with mathematics in any event. The only AI material is the UQ answers (Aug–Sep 2025) to a neighbouring question (uniformly supercompact cardinals), which conflict (o3 says yes, o4-mini says open, Gemini 2.5 Pro says inconsistent for the notion). Those answers are unvalidated by humans and are not in any result. Searches for Lean/AlphaProof/Aristotle/AlphaEvolve formalisations, Erdős-problem AI tracking, FrontierMath open problems, 2026 AI-math news, and the Woodin IAS April 2026 talk on AI and set theory (no transcript) turned up no AI contribution to this problem. Searches for MathOverflow, the 2026 Hausdorff Medal and the Moonlight review were not resolved (see incomplete).
competing_reading: (1) Jeon (2024) read as settling the consistency side: a nontrivial cofinal j: V→V is consistent with a ZF⁻-type theory relative to ZFC + I₀. Against: the v4 body's base theory includes the well-ordering principle, so the result may use choice; cofinality and the absence of Powerset are changes to the problem. (2) McCallum (2026) read as settling the non-existence side in ZF: a Σ₁ embedding of Vλ₊₃ inconsistent with ZF would refute Reinhardt-type embeddings via restriction, as Wikipedia reads it. Against: withdrawn by the author for an error in the proof; the Σ₁ Vλ₊₃ case is not V→V; the judging pass must decide whether a withdrawn claim counts. (3) Suzuki (1999) read as settling the question: a definable j is excluded in ZF, and Hamkins et al. say a definability-based refutation 'settles' the ZF(j) schema. Against: the bullet's j is not restricted to definable embeddings, and Hamkins et al. explicitly say the class case is open (Question 38). (4) Schlutzenberg's 2025 'Choice is necessary' claim read as answering the AC question in the negative for V→V. Against: conditional on I₀ consistency, about Vλ₊₂, and given only as talk abstracts.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A ZF(j) or NBG-without-AC proof that no nontrivial j: V→V exists (non-existence), or a consistency proof of one (existence), with the base theory and the scope of j stated. (b) For McCallum: the author's repaired version, or an expert verdict on the Skolem-function continuity step in the final section of 2601.10231v2, and whether any restriction from j: V→V to Vλ₊₃ is a valid route to the bullet. (c) For Jeon: the Fundamenta Mathematicae text's base theory for the main theorem (ZF⁻ with or without the well-ordering principle) and whether any choice principle is used. (d) For Schlutzenberg: the 2025 'recent work' the talk cites, if it is posted, and the publisher's dated JML page to settle the 2024 vs 2025 question. (e) For the Wikipedia Reinhardt page's 2025 Hausdorff claim: the European Set Theory Society's award page.
